pr_title: Bust the request cache when the mapping changes
pr_body:
This makes sure that we only serve a hit from the request cache if it
was build using the same mapping and that the entire search phase is
processed using the same mapping. These are both bugs that Elasticsearch
has had for a long, long time but now that we have runtime fields they
are much more likely to matter because runtime fields can be changed
*drastically* from moment to moment.

It does by adding a counter to the local mapping that is incremented
whenever the mapping changes. This counter and the mapping is stored
under a single `volatile` variable that is updated to point to the new
mapping whenever the mapping changes. When the search phase begins we
read the contents of the `volatile` and use it to power the entire
phase, and including the version counter into the cache key.

Before this change we'd go back to the `volatile` over and over again,
potentially getting a new version of the mapping every time. This was
convenient but made it possible that we'd see the mapping update half
way through the search phase which could cause trouble.

Mechanically, this creates a `snapshot()` method on `MapperService` to
do the volatile read of the current mapping. The snapshot does all of
the reading we need from here on out. I kept all of the methods on
`MapperService` that read directly from the mapping but deprecated all
of them because using them can lead to seeing the mapping updates when
you don't expect them. We can slowly remove the usages in follow up
changes. This change is big enough as is.

Sadly, the `Mapper`s are also mutable. Luckily, we only mutate them
before sticking them behind the `volatile` reference. Hopefully. There
is a lot of code there and it is hard to be sure. But it looks like we
*intend* to do this. We should make them properly immutable in a follow
up change.

Closes #62033
pr_comments: Creating as a draft so I can leave some comments and the robots can chew on it before I ping folks.

Sadly, this is the "small", "contained" version of this PR. There are probably a dozen follow ups that hint at wanting to be done. Things like:
* Make the entire mapping "obviously immutable" by using `final` variables and immutable objects. And removing all the `volatile` members. We *should* get the memory barrier by reading the snapshot.
* Shuffle other callers over to the snapshot. Things like the `get` and `term_vectors` APIs an indexing.
I'm going to work on merging master into this and getting the tests passing and *then* I'm going to see about forking it off into a different sort of cache busting that should be less controversial.

issue_context.title: Request cache and Runtime Fields
issue_context.body:
Modifications of Runtime Fields in the mapping should invalidate the request cache. Currently, search requests that target runtime fields are eligible to the request cache but they are not removed when a modification occurs. We consider this behavior as a non-released bug.
We discussed several solutions to this problem:

- Add a serializable mapping version in the shard search request cache key.

We already expose a mapping version that is incremented on each mapping update. However we don't force a single mapping version per request. The mapping service can be updated in the middle of the parsing of a search request so multiple versions of the mapping can co-exist in a single shard search request.
We could force a single version during the parsing but that would require to add a way to clone a mapping service so that's not a low hanging fruit.

- Add versioning for runtime fields that is plugged in the shard search request cache key.

With one version per field we could associate each runtime field used in the search request with its version. 
Although, extracting all fields that appear in a search request is not trivial. We don't have visitors for aggregations or query builders so that would require adding one. The advantage of this option is that caching would be invalidated only for search requests that target a modified runtime field.

- Invalidate all request cache entries whenever there is an update in the mapping.

Updating the mapping requires a cluster update so this event should be rare even with runtime fields.
We have plans to add the ability to plug runtime fields on top of the mapping (in the search request or in datastreams)
 in order to add more flexibility. For these reasons, a simple solution could be to invalidate the shard request cache entries whenever there is an update in the mapping. We already have this invalidation when the searcher reopens so that should be straightforward to add.

review_comments: this is some odd looking method, does it belong to the snapshot?

Its the name of the operation that we log when you merge something into the snapshot. Its `protected` so its part of the internal interface for snapshot and doesn't escape outside of `MapperService`. I kind of like that we can have the internal interface and the external one. Stuff like this that is convenient to push over to the snapshot we can push without it leaking.
I *think* putting the cache key into a local variable is safe here. It is quite large but we keep a reference to the key around for the entire request inside `cacheShardLevelResult` anyway.
And this is the important bit of the change - now QueryShardContext only references the snapshot.

I get nervous about deprecating all these methods. There are a ton of usages. I can see that it may be appealing to not introduce more, but we should also discuss how bad it is to not use the snapshot, and whether/how important it is to clean this up. I would not like to end up keeping all these deprecates methods for years. I can see how for instance field caps needs to be moved over like a lot of other consumers, although moving those over is not as important as it is for search. 

I was also wondering, could there be situations where seeing updates while they happen is a feature rather than a bug? I guess that your thinking is that it causes inconsistencies and a snapshot should always be used?

I feel like it'd be useful to think about all the callers, yeah. And I think if something really does want to constant get fresh snapshots it can have a `MapperService` and call `snapshot` over and over again.

I don't have to deprecate the methods but I think it's clearer when you read them from the snapshot. I'd feel better if we only had one method hiding a volatile read rather than a bunch of them.

Switching to a `DocumentMapper` was the smallest change I could make that got this to work, I think. I think I need to think more on this eventually because I don't want `documentMapper` to leak outside of `MapperService.Snapshot` but nested objects rely on it.

One option might be to have a `nestedDocuments(Function<Query, BitSetProducer> filterProducer)` method directly on Snapshot?  And then we could make NestedDocuments an interface and move all of the implementation details into DocumentMapper.
I was thinking that. If you'd like I can do that in this PR. I wasn't sure if we had other plans so I tried not to make this a big change to the file.
I believe I just replaced `mapperService` with `mapperService.snapshot()` but then I needed to fix the line length.
This change I think means that we will be able to remove this method subsequently, meaning that EmptySnapshot can be a singleton - see #63658
That'd be cool!
I don't think this can be changed via a merge, so maybe it doesn't belong on the Snapshot?
Oh but we need to refer to it through QueryShardContext, never mind.

One thing I struggle with: the volatile reference is for DocumentMapper. MapperService exposes functionalities around it and more. We end up snapshotting MapperService, and the snapshot holds methods that don't depend on DocumentMapper, hence are not affected by the volatile reference being swapped. I am referring to indexAnalyzers, parserContext and isMetadataField. These methods don't belong to the snapshot, but I guess we can't take them out unless we make their consumers depend on two things. Would it be worth it trying to address this if possible?

On this topic, have you experimented moving the methods that depend on Document mapper to document mapper? QueryShardContext could then have its own internal snapshot of document mapper, or even a direct final reference to it retrieved through MapperService that already exposes it? Maybe I am missing details around this, but I was wondering if this could be a good first step before we streamline using the snapshot more, as the main goal of this change is to make the query phase use the same mappings throughout its execution.

>  the snapshot holds methods that don't depend on DocumentMapper, hence are not affected by the volatile reference being swapped. I am referring to indexAnalyzers, parserContext and isMetadataField. These methods don't belong to the snapshot, but I guess we can't take them out unless we make their consumers depend on two things. Would it be worth it trying to address this if possible?

Yeah, I pushed the mutable bits together with the immutable bit because I figure it'd be convenient to depend on one "thing" for the mapping stuff. It feels convenient for `QueryShradContext`.

> On this topic, have you experimented moving the methods that depend on Document mapper to document mapper? QueryShardContext could then have its own internal snapshot of document mapper, or even a direct final reference to it retrieved through MapperService that already exposes it?

I poked at it a bit but didn't like the idea of adding the version to it because we'd have to move the merging stuff into it. And it felt better to leave it in MapperService.
I don't believe we need any BWC here because this doesn't escape the local node.

I certainly wondered the same. and I see that the common methods defined here are the parts that don't depend on document mapper and don't change over time, so I am wondering once more if we should try to do something about this. Is there a chance that we can get these methods out of the snapshot?

We can take the immutable ones out if you'd prefer. Its not a big thing to me either way. I'd want to make another interface or class for them or something. I don't want `QueryShardContext` to have a `MapperService` though so no one has to ask "does it just take the one snapshot or does it do it again?"
Moved to `QueryShardContext` which has the reference to the `documentMapper`.
When updating the mapping we now update the `Snapshot` reference which includes the mapping and the version number.
is it necessary to move the merge method to the snapshot? We could also merge the document mapper reference that it exposes, or what am I missing?
I moved it because it felt cleaner than the branch here. Without it i was doing a funny dance to make sure I only read the volatile one time.

Part of the issue is that at the time I was confused about whether or not `snapshot` could be null. I settled on "no". I started to like the idea of not having the null checks and instead having two "things", thus the two subclasses.
Any version will do!

This is the pattern that I use for most of these methods:
1. Copy them into the `Snapshot` interface.
2. Implement them.
3. Deprecate the original
4. Delegate to the snapshot.

I think we *can* remove all of these methods, but it'd make the PR quite large and we'd have to start thinking of stuff like `InternalEngine` and `IndexShard` and `TermVectorsService`. All things that probably could do with a second look to avoid all the volatile reads, but now is not the time.
This can no longer be null because we return it to query the mappings. All of the "empty mapping" handling logic is now in `EmptySnapshot` and the "normal" stuff is in `MappedSnapshot.`
can we list somewhere the follow-ups that we are planning like removing DocumentMapperForType as Alan suggested? Are there more?

If we're comfortable with the approach, yeah. But I don't think we're there yet. In my head it is mostly "trace the deprecated calls and see what we find". Maybe we find out that we want to be more careful and snapshot really early in a bunch of places. Maybe it isn't a big deal. But I'd like to look.

I think the other thing that we'd walk to follow up with is making the mapping "obviously immutable" in the java sense - removing the `volatile` variables from the mappers, stuff like that. I *think* we intend for the mapping to be entirely immutable and to commit changes via the MapperService.

I hinted at this as part of #64663 . Though most of the items in that issue are small-ish, while making object mapper and root object mapper immutable, get rid of cloning and all of the consequent changes, is a much bigger project. It probably makes sense to open a separate issue for that then.
